I am 62, I have a small household, and I already know the wheat-maize system well, so I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation and keep a smaller cotton area. With well irrigation and long experience, I am comfortable using improved or hybrid seed and moderate-to-strong fertilizer rates, but I do not want an overly complicated, high-risk plan. I will manage wheat for a steady winter crop, follow it with summer maize on the same land to make full use of the season, and keep cotton on a separate smaller block because it takes more labor and more pest control. I will use straightforward tillage, enough irrigation to protect yield, and a limited number of pesticide sprays focused on the likely pressure in each crop. My goal is reliable output and manageable labor rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
